name: Screen 2
prompt: Create a polished high-fidelity mobile article screen for the same news reader. At the top, show a simple article toolbar with a back chevron and “Top stories” on the left, and share and bookmark icon buttons on the right; the bookmark is unselected. Below, show the category label “WORLD”, the headline “Rescue teams search for survivors after powerful coastal quake”, a dek reading “Communities across the region are beginning to assess the damage as emergency crews work through the night.”, and metadata “By Elena Marquez · 8 min read · 24 min ago”. Add a wide dark image placeholder labeled “IMAGE — COASTAL QUAKE AFTERMATH”. Under it, show the caption “Residents gather near the harbor after the early-morning tremor.” Then render article body text with comfortable reading width: “Emergency crews moved into the hardest-hit coastal towns before sunrise Monday, searching damaged homes and clearing roads blocked by fallen masonry.”, “Officials said the strongest shock was followed by several aftershocks, but reported no immediate tsunami threat. Hospitals in three cities activated emergency plans as residents gathered in public squares.”, and “The full scale of the damage remains unclear. Local authorities asked people to conserve water and avoid damaged structures while assessment teams continue their work.” Add a light blue pull quote card reading “The first 24 hours are about reaching people safely and restoring the essential services they rely on.” End with “Reporting from Port Alira” in small muted text. Leave enough bottom padding for the shared navigation fragment.
jsx:
WORLD

Rescue teams search for survivors after powerful coastal quake

Communities across the region are beginning to assess the damage as emergency crews work through the night.

By Elena Marquez · 8 min read · 24 min ago

Emergency crews moved into the hardest-hit coastal towns before sunrise Monday, searching damaged homes and clearing roads blocked by fallen masonry.

Officials said the strongest shock was followed by several aftershocks, but reported no immediate tsunami threat. Hospitals in three cities activated emergency plans as residents gathered in public squares.

The full scale of the damage remains unclear. Local authorities asked people to conserve water and avoid damaged structures while assessment teams continue their work.

The first 24 hours are about reaching people safely and restoring the essential services they rely on.

Reporting from Port Alira
